# mod-spec

The spec is an **outline**: a map of the original that tells each porting agent what exists, what it must do and where in the Java to look. It is not a rewrite of the Java: the agents porting a block read its Java themselves (`make java-show`), after the outline. Existing specs (`planning/mods/redpower_2.md`, …) set the section order.

## Sections

1. **Overview & Version Target**: every version of the mod in our packs (version, pack, Minecraft version, archive under `assets/<pack>/`), the decompiled folder of each (`assets/decompiled/<archive>/`), and the original's **authors and licence**.
2. **Systems**: one short subsection per system (power network, microblocks, tubes, a VM…): what it does in a few sentences, its key numbers where they are easy to find, and the classes that hold it (`TileSolarPanel`, `BluePowerConductor`).
3. **Machines / devices**: per block: one or two lines on what it does, and its class.
4. **Tools, armor, items**: per item: one line, and its class.
5. **World generation & resources**: what generates, and the class.
6. **Complete registry**: tables of every block and item with the Rekkit id `<id>:<name>` and the original's id:meta.
7. **Recipes**: where they are registered (class and method); list the machine recipe types (`"<id>:<machine>"`).
8. **Hazards**: explosions, meltdowns, radiation, griefing, one line each.
9. **Hooks needed**: table of Horizon API level → entrypoint → feature (see horizon-hooks skill).
10. **Uses from rekkit_core**: the core types this mod relies on, and anything core lacks.
11. **Open questions**.

## Rules

- Decompile every version (`make decompile JAR=<archive>`, the client build when there is one) and read in pieces: `make java-outline DIR=assets/decompiled/<archive> ARGS=--classes` for the map, `GREP=<name>` for one class, `make java-show ... MEMBER=<Class#method>` for a method. Never a whole class, and each method once: the map pass reads only the class outline and the registry; each part's writer reads its part's methods once and writes everything from them.
- Name the class (and method, where it matters) for everything, so a porting agent can go straight to it.
- 1.2.5 and 1.4.7 mods use numeric block/item ids and damage values: record the original id:meta next to each registry row.
- **Several versions: merge, newer wins.** When a mod ships in more than one pack (RedPower 2.0pr5b2 in Tekkit 1.2.5 and 2.0pr6 in Direwolf20 1.4.7), the port is the union of every version: each block, item, recipe and system any version has. Where versions share a feature, the newest version's behaviour, numbers and art win (both have the alarm: the 1.4.7 alarm). A feature only an older version has stays, as that version made it (1.2.5's microblocks stay even if 1.4.7 dropped them). Tag each registry row and system with the version it comes from (`[2.0pr6]`), and add a **Versions** table: feature → versions that have it → version used. One merged mod, never one per version.
- **Uses from rekkit_core**: something belongs in the core when another ported or queued mod needs it too (name those mods); the conductor files each lack with `make core-need`.

## Outline file and contracts

End step 1 with `planning/mods/<id>.features.json`, the outline the conductor makes beads from (`make fleet-features MOD=<id>`): every block, item and subsystem, and for each block and item its **attributes**, the things a player must find it doing (`"generates power in daylight"`, `"stores energy"`, `"opens a 3x3 crafting GUI"`, `"reads voltage on right-click"`). Every attribute is a blocker until a scenario tests it.

The agent porting a block or item writes its **contract file**, `planning/mods/<id>.contract/<name>.json`, from the Java before it builds anything: what the original is, so a port that only places, opens a stock grid and drops cannot pass. One file per block or item, so parallel agents never edit the same file; its fields are merged over the outline's entry. `make contract-check MOD=<id>` (and `check-mods COMPLETE=1`) compares the port's models and textures with it pixel for pixel and fails on any untested attribute; the live harness checks its GUI, shape and scenarios. Outline, then contract fields, shown merged:

```json
{
  "blocks": [{
    "id": "alloy_furnace", "name": "Alloy Furnace", "java": "BlockAppliance meta 0",
    "shape": "full",
    "facing": "horizontal",
    "faces": {"top": "eloraam/base/base1.png#19", "front": "eloraam/base/base1.png#17",
              "side": "eloraam/base/base1.png#16", "bottom": "eloraam/base/base1.png#16"},
    "gui": {"size": [176, 166], "title": "Alloy Furnace",
            "slots": [[48, 17], [66, 17], [84, 17], [48, 35], [66, 35], [84, 35], [48, 53], [66, 53], [84, 53], [17, 42], [141, 35]]},
    "energy": null,
    "attributes": ["L3: smelts alloys from a 3x3 input with solid fuel", "L5: keeps its items and progress when its chunk reloads",
                   "L6: takes inputs from the top and fuel from the front"]
  }, {
    "id": "and_gate", "name": "AND Gate", "java": "BlockLogic meta 1 (RenderLogic)",
    "shape": [0, 0, 0, 16, 2, 16], "facing": "horizontal",
    "faces": {"top": "eloraam/logic/logic1.png#2", "side": "eloraam/logic/logic1.png#0"}, "gui": null,
    "attributes": ["L4: outputs redstone only when both inputs are on"]
  }],
  "items": [{"id": "voltmeter", "name": "Voltmeter", "java": "ItemVoltmeter",
             "sprite": "eloraam/base/items1.png#24", "max_stack": 1, "durability": null,
             "use": "right-click a blutricity block: chat 'Reading %.2fV %.2fA (%.2fW)'"}],
  "features": [{"id": "blutricity_grid", "name": "Blutricity power network", "spec": "3.5"}],
  "scenarios": [{"name": "solar panel charges in daylight", "for": ["solar_panel", "voltmeter"], "level": 3,
                 "covers": ["generates power in daylight", "stores energy"], "steps": [
    {"command": "time set noon"}, {"setblock": [0, 0, 0, "redpower_2:solar_panel"]}, {"wait": 200},
    {"use": "redpower_2:voltmeter", "on": [0, 0, 0]},
    {"expect_message": "Reading (?!0\\.00V)\\d+\\.\\d\\dV"}]}]
}
```

In a contract file, `scenarios` is a list like the one above (its `for` defaults to the file's block or item). Every block needs `shape`, `facing`, `faces` and `gui`; every item `sprite` and `max_stack`; every attribute a scenario whose `covers` names it. Where to find each in the original:

- **shape**: `"full"`, or the outline of its default state as `/setblock` places it, `[x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2]` in pixels (0-16), from `setBlockBounds` (a gate or plate `[0,0,0,16,2,16]`, a wire, a panel). Plants: `"cross"`.
- **facing**: `"horizontal"` or `"all"` when it turns to the player as placed (`onBlockPlacedBy` storing a direction), `"none"` otherwise.
- **faces**: the sprite on each face as placed facing north: `top`, `bottom`, `front` (north), `back`, `left`, `right`, `side` (every side not named), `all`; from `getBlockTextureFromSideAndMetadata`/`getBlockTexture` and the block's texture file. A sprite is `"<sheet path in the archive>#<index>"` (index = row × 16 + column on a 16-wide sheet), as in `asset-map.json`'s slices; `"minecraft:block/<name>"` when the original reuses a vanilla texture. Name every face the original draws, also on a model drawn by code (`RenderLogic`, a TESR): its base, plate or top sprite.
- **gui**: `null` when right-clicking opens nothing; else its `Gui*` class's `xSize`/`ySize` as `size`, and the position of each of the block's own slots in its `Container*` (the `new Slot(inv, n, x, y)` calls, without the player's inventory), in slot order.
- **energy**: `null`, or `{"role": "producer|consumer|storage|conductor"}`.
- **items**: `sprite` from `setIconIndex`/`iconIndex` and the item's texture file (a list for subtypes: one sprite each); `max_stack` from `setMaxStackSize` (64 if never set); `durability` from `setMaxDamage` (null if none); `use` what right-clicking does, in your words.
- **scenarios**: one at least for every outlined attribute (`covers`), and for every machine, generator, tool and item that does something a player sees: what goes in, how long, and what the player can read afterwards (a chat line, a block state, `data get block`). Steps: `setblock [dx,dy,dz,block]`, `command`, `wait` (ticks), `use` (an item on a block `on [dx,dy,dz]`), `interact [dx,dy,dz]`, and checks `expect_message` (regex on chat and the action bar), `expect_block [dx,dy,dz,regex]` (its state), `expect_data [dx,dy,dz,regex]`. Write the expectation from the original's numbers and messages, never from the port.

## Test levels

Every attribute has a level, and a scenario of that level must pass (`"level"` on the scenario, the attribute's text in its `covers`). An untested or failing attribute is a blocker.

| Level | What it proves | Who checks it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Placement & hitbox | placed by `/setblock` and by a player in every variant, outline = the original's shape, faces the player | the harness, for every block |
| 2 Item use | a tool breaks what it should and loses durability, an item carries its NBT/components (charge, colour), right-click effects | a scenario for every item with a `use` or durability |
| 3 Block function | energy (generates, stores, consumes), fuel, storage, the GUI's slots doing their job (fuel slot takes fuel, output slot refuses input), progress | a scenario for every block with a GUI or energy |
| 4 Interaction | with other blocks: wires carry power or signal to machines, tubes deliver, gates respond to inputs, machines push and pull | a scenario for each such attribute |
| 5 Persistence | the chunk reloaded from disk (`{"reload_chunk": true}`): state, inventory and energy kept | a scenario for every block with a GUI or energy |
| 6 Automation & sides | hoppers and tubes insert and extract through the original's sided access | a scenario for each sided block |
| 7 All mods together | the all-mods harness phase: no conflicts with other mods | `make e2e-all-mods` |

Scenario steps beyond the ones above: `{"ctl": ["inventory"], "expect": "\"damage\": 1"}` runs any horizon-ctl command (`{x}` `{y}` `{z}` in its words become the scenario's position, `"at"` offsets it) and matches its JSON reply; `{"reload_chunk": true}` saves, drops and reloads the patch's chunk.

## Tickets

In part mode each spec-writer reads its part of the decompiled code (`make fleet-parts MOD=<id>`) once and writes, in its own files, the part's outline (`planning/mods/<id>.parts/<part>.md`, `###` headings), its blocks' and items' attributes (`planning/mods/<id>.parts/<part>.features.json`) and its tickets (`planning/mods/<id>.tickets/<part>.json`). `make fleet-tickets MOD=<id>` merges the parts into the spec (under "Part details") and the outline, validates every part together and files the tickets in Beads with their order; `make fleet-dispatch` works them. `make fleet-tickets SCHEMA=1` prints the format.

```json
{"tickets": [{
  "key": "part12-solar-panel", "title": "Solar panel: model, generation, storage",
  "role": "domain-builder-pro", "step": 3, "effort_k": 120,
  "covers": ["solar_panel"],
  "files": ["mods/redpower_2/src/blutricity/solar.rs", "planning/mods/redpower_2.contract/solar_panel.json"],
  "spec": ["2.5 Blutricity Power Grid"], "java": ["TileSolarPanel#updateEntity", "BlockMachinePanel#getBlockTexture"],
  "after": ["part12-bluewire-grid"],
  "description": "What to build and how it behaves, in a few sentences. Done: make contract-check clean for solar_panel; its level 1, 3 and 5 scenarios pass."
}]}
```

- **Size**: `effort_k` aimed at 200 at most (thousand tokens: one agent's context, reading included), and at most 6 `files` and 8 `spec` headings plus `java` members. What costs is turns: each file written and each thing read is about one, and every turn re-sends all the context before it, so an agent wraps up at 25 turns or 500k tokens billed. Bigger work is several tickets in order.
- **Reads**: the ticket's agent gets the text of every spec heading and Java member it names in its brief (`make fleet-task`), so name exactly what it needs: the method, not the class.
- **Role**: content-author, domain-builder, domain-builder-pro, hook-engineer, test-smith, asset-smith, scaffolder or scribe. The ticket's role writes the contract file of what it covers if nobody has.
- **Order**: `after` lists the keys that must be closed first. Whatever a ticket uses (the grid, a core type, a block's content before its GUI) comes before it; two tickets editing the same file are ordered (lang, creative tab and tag files excepted). No cycles.
- **Coverage**: every block, item and subsystem of the outline is in some ticket's `covers`.
- **Description**: enough for an agent that has read nothing else: what, where, which spec sections and Java methods, and what done means.
